The NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NCAT) decides a range of civil and administrative cases in New South Wales. NCAT commenced operation on 1 January 2014, consolidating the work of 22 former tribunals into a single point of access for specialist tribunal services in NSW. The Civil and Administrative Tribunal Act 2013 establishes NCAT and governs its operations.

NCAT provides a simple, quick and effective process for resolving disputes and reviewing administrative action. Its supports include services and processes for self-representation in most matters, plain-language forms and documents, simplified processes, and alternative dispute resolution methods. Its broad range of cases includes tenancy issues, building works, guardianship decisions, and administrative review of government decisions. NCAT generally manages its broad jurisdiction and case types through its Divisions. Its Appeal Panel provides a timely and cost-effective mechanism for prompt reviews of most Tribunal decisions.

NCAT's jurisdiction and diverse case types are generally managed through four Divisions and the Appeal Panel. To apply, a person first identifies the case type and completes an application form. After receiving a notice of hearing, a party should begin preparing. NCAT uses alternative resolution processes to help parties settle disputes before a hearing. Parties can find out what to expect when arriving for a hearing or other listing event. After a hearing, NCAT makes a decision and orders. Certain Tribunal decisions can be internally appealed to the NCAT Appeal Panel.

NCAT's Consumer and Commercial Division resolves everyday disputes, including tenancy and other residential disputes and consumer claims. Its case types include housing and property matters: tenancy, social housing, boarding houses, residential communities, holiday parks, agricultural tenancy, strata schemes, community schemes, home building, retirement villages, and dividing fences. It also deals with consumers and businesses matters: consumer claims, motor vehicles, retail leases, agent commissions and fees, conveyancing costs, pawnbrokers, and second-hand dealers.
records.topic: Consumer and Commercial Division case types

records.text: The NCAT Appeal Panel determines internal appeals from decisions made by NCAT's Divisions. It hears internal appeals from decisions of each Division where a right of appeal is provided under the Civil and Administrative Tribunal Act 2013 (NCAT Act) or enabling legislation. It also hears designated external appeals provided for by the NCAT Act or enabling legislation. Before proceeding with an appeal or seeking leave to appeal, a person should read the NCAT Guideline on Internal Appeals and consult information about making an internal appeal.

A person can apply to NCAT to make certain decisions, review decisions, or resolve a dispute. NCAT handles everyday issues including tenancy and building-work disputes, guardianship decisions, and administrative review of government decisions. Application processes vary by case type, and time limits may apply; applicants should select the case type that best describes their dispute or issue.

To start proceedings at NCAT, an applicant completes an application form and lodges it with the appropriate fee. Forms are available as downloadable fillable PDFs, and some application types can be filed online. Applications require the applicant's and other party's names and contact details, the orders sought, and reasons for seeking those orders. For an urgent issue, applicants should consult the process for applying for an urgent hearing.

An NCAT application fee may be payable depending on case type; eligible people may receive a reduced concession fee. Time limits may apply, and applicants should check the information for their case type. For an application against a business or company, the applicant must provide the name of the individual or company that owns the business, the registered name and address, its ABN or ACN, and a business-name or company extract to NCAT.
